RU-21-02-0173-310822/FACTSHEET 
 
 
 
 
 
 
‘One Nation One Ration Card’ 
 
Making food security portable throughout the country 
 
100% Digitisation of Ration Cards 
 
(Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution) 
 
August 31, 2022 
 
“With the help of One Nation-One Ration Card, we have ensured free ration to more than 
80 crore countrymen. This is the wonder of technology.” 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Prime Minister, Narendra Modi 
One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) is a technology-driven scheme which is being 
implemented by the Central Government for the nationwide portability of ration cards under 
the National Food Security Act (NFSA).1 To address the difficulties of migrants, this system 
for intra-State and inter-State portability of ration cards was launched by the Government of 
India on August 09, 2019.2 
 
ONORC is a countrywide innovation that allows all NFSA beneficiaries, particularly migrant 
beneficiaries, to claim either full or part foodgrains from any Fair Price Shop (FPS) of their 
choice in the country through the existing ration card with biometric/Aadhaar authentication in 
 
1 Factsheet Details: (pib.gov.in) 
2 https://transformingindia.mygov.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/ONORC-eng.pdf

a seamless manner. The system also allows their family members back home, if any, to claim 
the balance of foodgrains on same the ration card.3 
At present, ONORC is effectively implemented in all 36 States and Union Territories, 
making food security portable throughout the country, with Assam becoming the last state to 
have it implemented.4 
 
 
Genesis5 
The One Nation One Ration Card reform has its genesis in the vision that the computerisation 
of the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) in the country must be taken to the next 
level in ensuring food security in the country. 
This system enables migrant beneficiaries to seamlessly get their food grains from any Fair Price 
Shop of their choice, in any part of the country, by using their same/existing ration card with 
biometric authentication of identity on an ePoS device. 
This initiative also provides leverage to States/UTs to serve many more beneficiaries, without 
actually incurring any additional burden. Furthermore, this mechanism can plug the 
leakage/diversion of un-lifted food grains in FPSs, as they can now be lifted by their rightful 
beneficiaries through portability and get reconciled/ adjusted between States/UTs, thereby 
minimizing the chances of un-lifted foodgrains getting diverted.

❖ ONORC 
uses

‘Right to Food’ with the concept of 5R’s

Right Beneficiary at Right Time at Right 
Fair Price. 
❖ ONORC had become an integral part of 
“Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna 
Yojana” to distribute free commodities to 
migrants during Covid-19. 
❖ Key components are National Portability, 
de-duplication of beneficiaries, creation of 
ration card-Central Repository and Data 
analytics.

Progress of One Nation One Ration Card implementation in States/UTs 
 
 
Progress of NFSA Population Coverage under ONORC 
 
 
❖ 80 Crore beneficiaries avail benefit of ONORC, recording nearly three crore portability 
transactions per month.8 
 
❖ The Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD) received the Prime Minister’s 
Award for Excellence in Public Administration, 2020 for the ‘One Nation One Ration 
Card’ scheme.9 
 
❖ The Department is collaborating with other Ministries/Departments to leverage the 
ONORC database for deepening the outreach of citizen-centric government schemes 
across the country. 10
